season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.detail: Audit was right: my 80% threshold was the expired 2020/2022 waiver. Re-verified from NCAA primary text: 2025-26 Postseason Bowl Handbook (Bylaw 18.7.2) says one FCS win counts only if the opponent 'averaged 90 percent of the permissible maximum number of grants-in-aid' over a rolling two-year period, with a waiver for catastrophic cases; Feb 2026 House-settlement Q&A B7 puts it at 56.7 per year; deserving = FBS wins >= overall losses; a deserving team losing its title game stays deserving. June 2026 DI Cabinet report (ncaaorg S3 PDF) lists 2026-30 and 2026-31 'Adopted. (Final)'. Re-patched cfb.bowl_selection_state mechanism/rationale/measurement/raw_data/free_sources (input_patches/CFB_a.json) to 90%/56.7 and the handbook rules; season_futures stage s7, required_data and unresolved text corrected; no '80%' or 'obsolete 90%' remains outside the season_futures new_inputs copy, which apply_patches overwrites.

season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.detail: Duplicate confirmed (catalog already carried audit_flag DUPLICATE on cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features). Canonical = cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model: patch merges the feature lists (head-to-head, common opponents, QB injury flag, SOS, pre/post-championship weights, pairwise-ordering calibration, per-release rank output); cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features patched to an alias definition. In the unreg:polls_and_cfp_rankings record the duplicate was removed from new_inputs, audited DUPLICATE_OF:cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model, and every stage/coverage/interaction/required_data reference swapped to the canonical id, which is added as a primary input there; cfb.title_path_to_final_ap measurement patched to cite it. Follow-up for the audit's leftovers: archetype_patches/CFB_a.json detaches the alias from unreg:polls_and_cfp_rankings. The canonical input's raw_data/free_sources gain a point-in-time QB availability source. Catalog interactions that still name the alias id cannot be edited by the patch tools; they resolve to the alias definition.

touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.detail: Verified 2026-11-08 on the Kalshi public series API: no CFB named-player TD series exists (only TEAMTD, TOTALTD, TEAMRSHTD, TEAMRECTD, DSTTD, FIRSTTDTEAM; the NFL has KXNFLANYTD/FIRSTTD). series_assignment.json already re-filed all six to game_stat_props and the touchdown_scorer record is NO_LIVE_SERIES with player inputs audited WEAK, but the catalog game_stat_props entry lacked the TD-count inputs. Fixed: game_stat_props record new_inputs now attach cfb.td_per_scoring_trip, cfb.td_count_dispersion, cfb.dst_td_propensity, cfb.first_td_race_rate and cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix as primary (identical definitions, merged by integrate); player_series_missing text updated to the dormant state.  Follow-up: archetype_patches/CFB_a.json demotes td_rates and player_usage to secondary and team_total_split to context, and marks the target dormant.

unreg:team_event_counting_specials#stat_.detail: Duplicate confirmed: cfb.opp_dropback_volume is cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts (dropbacks = attempts plus sacks, script-adjusted, already with opponent pass-rate-allowed term) evaluated for the opposing offence. Consolidated: removed from team_event_counting_specials new_inputs and audited DUPLICATE_OF:cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts there and in unreg:season_stat_leader (was KEEP_SECONDARY); all stage, coverage, interaction, nonlinearity and required_data references swapped; canonical input attached to team_event_counting_specials as primary with an opponent-view why; cfb.opp_dropback_volume patched to an alias definition. The archetype split itself (yards/TDs in game_stat_props, sacks/INT/FG/2PT/delay here) matches series_assignment.json. Follow-up: archetype_patches/CFB_a.json detaches cfb.opp_dropback_volume from team_event_counting_specials and season_stat_leader. The record catalog_entry now uses the canonical id, and the stale alias rationale is patched. Catalog interactions naming the alias id remain (they can't be patched).
